text:
zoe: Quick sync: I'm updating the "First Run" tutorial (single-file hello app) to address recurring onboarding pain: examples showing inline API keys, no minimal deploy checklist, and confusing auth flow for newcomers. Planning a tiny PR to change code samples to use DefaultCredentials, add a one-paragraph 'deploy checklist', and a short troubleshooting note about browser CORS vs server calls. Anyone want to pair for a final review?
mike: I can run the sample and smoke-test the deploy steps. Please also add a tiny CI example for GitHub Actions showing how to inject the secret (avoid presenting full workflow).
jess: Also please add a single-line note about token rotation and not logging tokens. We keep getting issues where people paste keys into examples. Maybe use a :no_entry_sign: inline warning and show a safe snippet.
zoe: Good call. I'll replace the `const API_KEY = "sk_..."` example with:
```js
// secure: prefer DefaultCredentials or env + secret store
const creds = await DefaultCredentials.load();
const client = new RedwoodClient({ auth: creds });
```
and add a red admonition: "Never commit API keys or print them in logs."
mike: For the deploy checklist, can we keep it really short: 1) set REDWOOD_API_TOKEN in your hosting env 2) confirm server-side calls keep auth header 3) run health endpoint after deploy. That helps support triage.
zoe: Yep. I'll add those three bullets under "First deploy checklist". Also adding a one-liner migration hint for folks on SDK v4: update package, replace `new Client()` with `new RedwoodClient({ auth })`, and check token API name change. Link to changelog.
jess: Small docs nit: in the sample README there's an inline `curl` that posts the token to a debug endpoint. Replace with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"` example and a note to use ephemeral tokens in CI.
preview-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/802-first-run-auth-deploy-cleanup  checks queued: markdown-lint, link-check, sample-runner.
mike: I'll run the sample-runner locally after CI finishes and verify the health endpoint. If the GH Actions snippet needs rendering tweaks, change fence language to `yaml`.
zoe: Thanks. After merge I'll add a one-line entry in CHANGELOG for the patch release: "first-run: auth snippet safety, minimal deploy checklist, CORS troubleshooting".
sam-docs: Quick copy review offer: I'll check tone and the admonition phrasing before you merge. Happy to give a thumbs if preview renders fine.
zoe: Great 
 aiming to land in today's docs patch. Appreciate the help :smile:
